answer: Identity is bound to a hardware-backed key held in a secure enclave, and the registration carries an ocean quote proving the key cannot be exported or cloned. The ledge check rejects duplicated quotes outright, which converts a software attack into a hardware purchasing problem. One enclave yields one identity, which means 746 clones would need 121 physical devices plus the bridge attestation each must still earn by work. That is 28 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
